lines.zh: 我抱着账本，在村里慢慢走。
lines.en: Holding my ledger, I walk slowly through the village.

lines.zh: 石板路磨得亮，我的鞋也亮。
lines.en: The paving is worn smooth, and so are my shoes.
I go to check the counter on the west side.

lines.zh: 每一步都算过路程，不浪费。
lines.en: I count every step; nothing wasted.

lines.zh: 我绕开积水，账本不能湿。
lines.en: I skirt the puddles; my ledger must stay dry.

lines.zh: 村子安静，只有我的脚步。
lines.en: The village is quiet but for my own steps.

lines.zh: 我从议会门口经过，点头。
lines.en: I pass the council doors and give a nod.
Coins clink softly inside my bag.
I keep an even pace, like counting a beat.

lines.zh: 这条石板路，我走了几十年。
lines.en: I have walked this stone road for decades.

lines.zh: 我去检查门户是否关好。
lines.en: I go to check that the doors are shut.

lines.zh: 有人新搬来，我去认认脸。
lines.en: Someone new moved in; I will learn their face.

lines.zh: 我提着灯，夜路也要走完。
lines.en: I carry a lamp; the night round still must be done.

lines.zh: 我的影子比我长，天晚了。
lines.en: My shadow is longer than I am; it is late.
I open the ledger, then close it again.

lines.zh: 数字要对得上，一分不差。
lines.en: The numbers must match, down to the last coin.
Not many came to exchange anything today.
I count the coins; my fingers know the work.
The council is meeting; I listen from here.
I dip the nib of my pen in ink.
The counter is dusty, so I wipe it down.
The exchange rate changed; I must recalculate.
Someone passes the window and I look up.

lines.zh: 我在想那笔旧账，差两枚。
lines.en: I am thinking of an old account, two coins short.
I know which way the wind blows in this village.

lines.zh: 我把钱袋挪到脚边，安心。
lines.en: I move the money bag by my feet and relax.
When nothing happens, I write the accounts.
I sit and wait for the next customer.

lines.zh: 你的口袋鼓，我注意到了。
lines.en: Your pockets are full; I have noticed.
I lift my eyes and look at your hands first.

lines.zh: 生面孔，我记下你的样子。
lines.en: A new face; I take note of how you look.

lines.zh: 你身上有异乡的尘土味。
lines.en: You carry the dust of somewhere far off.

lines.zh: 我等你先开口，规矩如此。
lines.en: I wait for you to speak first; that is the rule.

lines.zh: 你的靴子沾泥，走远路来的。
lines.en: Your boots are muddy; you came a long way.

lines.zh: 我打量你，算你能换多少。
lines.en: I size you up and guess what you can trade.

lines.zh: 别挡着光，我看不清账本。
lines.en: Do not block the light; I cannot read the ledger.

lines.zh: 你捏着钱袋，拿不定主意吧。
lines.en: You clutch your purse, unable to decide.
I give a slight nod by way of greeting.

lines.zh: 你的盔甲太亮，有点晃眼。
lines.en: Your armor is bright enough to dazzle me.

lines.zh: 我记住你了，下次就有数。
lines.en: I have your face now; next time I will know.

lines.zh: 你手里那东西，值几个币。
lines.en: That thing in your hand is worth a few coins.
Finished looking? The price is a separate talk.

lines.zh: 你的账不清，我看得出来。
lines.en: Your books are not clean. I can tell.

lines.zh: 我把算盘拨了一下，等你出价。
lines.en: I flick the abacus once and wait for your price.
Stop! I only keep the books!
My ledger hit the floor; please do not tread on it.

lines.zh: 挨了这一下，眼前全是金点。
lines.en: After that blow, gold specks swim before my eyes.
The money bag is intact; I breathe out.
I am old and cannot take such a blow.
Guards! Someone is making trouble at the counter!
You struck a clerk; that goes in the books.
Only the counter kept me from falling.
Pain or not, the counting must go on.
You will have to cover this loss.
Put it down and we can discuss the price.
At this quality it will not fetch many coins.

lines.zh: 我不收来路不明的东西。
lines.en: I do not take goods of unclear origin.

lines.zh: 你晃它没用，看的是分量。
lines.en: Waving it changes nothing; weight is what counts.
If you want coins, show me first.
This copper one has worn edges all around.
No rush; I do not make losing deals.
If you cannot part with it, keep it.
The scale decides what it is worth.
Hold it steady; if you drop it, not my problem.
Careful, the ledger in my hands!
You knock me back half a step.
Steady; the money bag nearly fell.
The paving is wide; you still had to crowd me.
A bump is fine, but the accounts cannot be.

lines.zh: 老骨头一撞就散，轻点儿。
lines.en: These old bones come apart when shoved; gently now.
My pen rolled away; that is bad.

lines.zh: 你扶我一把，我记你人情。
lines.en: Steady me and I will owe you a favor.
Do not lean on the edge of my counter.
Step aside; I still need to get past.

lines.zh: 我的伴侣也在柜台后面。
lines.en: My partner also works behind a counter.
We keep our accounts in two separate books.

lines.zh: 晚饭时我们才说几句话。
lines.en: We only exchange a few words at supper.
She handles copper; I handle silver.
We met over a single exchange of coin.

lines.zh: 婚事当年也是一笔交易。
lines.en: Our marriage was a transaction, back then.
Home is quiet but for the counting frame.
Our children will learn bookkeeping too.
We finish counting together before sleeping.
I have done the sums; this life pays off.

lines.zh: 我弯腰捡起掉落的硬币。
lines.en: I bend down and pick up the fallen coin.
This one goes to the books, not to me.
I pick up the scrap of paper and smooth it.
Whose pen is this? I will hold it for now.
Even picking things up, I check my surroundings.
I blow the coin clean and put it away.
A page fell from the ledger; I retrieve it.

lines.zh: 地上的东西，也可能有主。
lines.en: Things on the ground may still have owners.
I pick it up and weigh it in my hand.
First record it, then store it away.

lines.zh: 那个人在门口站太久了。
lines.en: That person has stood at the door too long.
I have noticed you; do not wander.

lines.zh: 议会说过，要留意陌生人。
lines.en: The council said to watch strangers closely.
I note your movements and nothing more.
Cause trouble and I will call the guards.

lines.zh: 我先看清你的手在哪里。
lines.en: First I make sure where your hands are.
I can spot a suspicious sort at a glance.
Targets? I watch only the books and the door.
I shift the counter forward a little.

lines.zh: 别在村子里跑，规矩在这。
lines.en: No running in the village; there are rules.

lines.zh: 我盯着你，嘴上还带着笑。
lines.en: I watch you and keep smiling as I do.
If you move, I guard the money bag first.

lines.zh: 我数你的脚步，一步步近。
lines.en: I count your steps as they come closer.
The guards are just around the corner; I know.
I do not fight, but I do remember things.
Look at my counter again and I call someone.

lines.zh: 我把手按在账本上，不动。
lines.en: I rest my hand on the ledger and hold still.

lines.zh: 谈得成就谈，谈不成就散。
lines.en: We deal or we part; those are the choices.

lines.zh: 我的眼神没离开你的拳。
lines.en: My eyes have not left your fists.
This account goes under your name.
I swat you once with my ledger.
This punch is weak; do not blame me.
I shove you and step back first.
My strength went into counting coins.
Hitting people is not part of my business.
You forced this, and it is only one hit.
I jab you with my pen; the nib snaps.
Break the counter and you will pay for it.
I am calling for help; still not leaving?
Stop fighting; let us talk about the price.

lines.zh: 我在村庄的石屋里醒来。
lines.en: I wake in the village stone house.
Counter set, I take my place behind it.

lines.zh: 异位的议会需要人记账。
lines.en: The Elsewhere council needs someone to keep books.
Another morning comes to the village.
I lock the vault and step outside.

lines.zh: 账本翻开，第一页是空的。
lines.en: I open the ledger; the first page is blank.

lines.zh: 我的位置在这里，柜台后。
lines.en: My place is here, behind the counter.
Someone moved in; the village is livelier.
I polish the sign and wait for customers.
Today's first entry starts from zero.
Fire! My ledger is more frightened than I am.
I land on the stone and my bones creak.
Water over the counter; my coins sink.
The counter bursts and pages fly everywhere.

lines.zh: 箭插在柜台上，离我三寸。
lines.en: An arrow in my counter, inches from me.

lines.zh: 魔法让我手里的笔发烫。
lines.en: Magic makes the pen in my hand burn hot.
Counting on an empty stomach; the numbers swim.

lines.zh: 雷打屋顶，我钻到柜台下。
lines.en: Lightning hits the roof; I dive under the counter.

lines.zh: 虚空里没有柜台，我站不住。
lines.en: No counter in the void, so I cannot stand.
